extracted.intended_audience: general public; potential grantees, partners, and stakeholders seeking information about the Ford Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational overview of the Ford Foundation describing its mission, history, governance, policies, regional presence, and approaches to grantmaking and stewardship. Useful for potential applicants, partners, and stakeholders wanting to understand the foundation's priorities and structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission and core goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Our mission has sought to reduce poverty and injustice, strengthen democratic values, promote international cooperation, and advance human achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Across nine decades the foundation's social justice mission and vision guide its work and transformations in the foundation and the communities it serves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from Ford Motor Company
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ford Foundation is not connected to the Ford Motor Company. The Ford Foundation and Ford Motor Company are two separate and legally unrelated entities whose operations are completely independent and have been for more than 50 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is not any financial authority, decision making nor funding relationship between the two organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance and leadership expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation is governed by a distinguished and diverse Board of Trustees, which includes our president. Our grant making is led by directors and regional representatives with expertise in their fields and a profound commitment to social change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantmaking decisions are overseen by experienced leadership and a board responsible for governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding policies for operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Our operations are guided by a set of policies relating to grant making, geographic focus, spending, investment, management, governance, and professional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policies direct how the foundation approaches grants, geographical priorities, budgeting and investments, management practices, governance, and professional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe in transparency—both within the foundation and in philanthropy at large—and have made available extensive information about our governance, operations, and finances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation provides access to governance policies and financial statements to promote transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endowment stewardship and long-term sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn what makes us different from public charities, where our original endowment came from, and how—through careful stewardship of our assets—we will be able to keep our mission alive for years to come.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation emphasizes careful management of its endowment to ensure ongoing capacity to fund mission-aligned work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority to ensure grantees have needed resources
rubrics_metrics.description: In all our investments and budgeting, our highest priority is making sure that our grantees have the resources they need to address today’s most pressing challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgeting and investment decisions are oriented toward supporting grantee capacity to tackle urgent problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local engagement (Good Neighbor Committee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1996, the foundation’s Good Neighbor Committee has supported organizations and activities near our headquarters, in the Midtown Manhattan area of New York, that contribute to the neighborhood’s civic spirit and vitality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee’s work strengthens ties to immediate neighbors and connects to local organizations; some regional offices have formed similar Good Neighbor Committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic presence and regional offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation maintains offices and regional representation across multiple regions (United States, Mexico and Central America, Brazil, Andean Region, Middle East and North Africa, East Africa, China, Southern Africa, West Africa, India/Nepal/Sri Lanka, Indonesia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional offices provide local contacts and reflect the foundation's geographic focus and capacity for regionally-relevant work.
